commentary.bottom_line: Nine sources, including CHAI playbooks, FDA draft lifecycle guidance, and the HEAAL framework, endorse naming an owner and running a recurring, resourced process for AI bias evaluation, but no supplied study tests whether doing so reduces biased outputs or disparate outcomes. The recommendation rests on expert consensus and regulatory direction rather than measured effect.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests an assigned owner or recurring lifecycle process for bias management, and no study documents the hazard itself. The endorsements come from frameworks, guidance, and commentaries. Under GRADE conventions, consensus statements do not establish certainty of effect, so the size and direction of any benefit remain unknown.

FDA draft guidance on AI-enabled device software asks that bias control be built in from the earliest design stage through decommission across the total product lifecycle. This is a draft and applies to device manufacturers, so it may shape vendor expectations more directly than hospital governance duties. No supplied study measures compliance or its effects.

The HEAAL framework and the related action guide organize equity review across adoption stages and five domains, including accountability and fairness. These documents describe procedures but report no evaluation of whether they change outcomes for Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients.

The recommendation calls for defined roles and resources, yet no supplied source reports staffing levels, cost, or time needed to sustain recurring bias reviews. Health systems would need to estimate these burdens locally until implementation data become available.

commentary.research_gap: Studies should compare health systems or deployments with and without a designated bias owner and scheduled lifecycle reviews, measuring detection of performance gaps across patient subgroups, time to remediation, and changes in disparate outcomes, along with the staffing and cost of maintaining the process.
commentary.underserved_note: No supplied study tested the practice in any population, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Whether a governance owner and recurring review detect or correct bias affecting these groups is currently unmeasured.
